coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Parcel K North (PKN)
record.summary: The 1.5-acre former Port parking lot at 20th and Illinois Streets, sold in February 2019 to a TMG Partners / Presidio Bay Ventures joint venture under a Vertical DDA after a competitive offering, generating $24.2 million of land proceeds for the Pier 70 project. Planning approved a 65-ft, 245-unit for-sale condominium building over ground-floor retail (377,506 gsf, Handel Architects) in November 2019; as of 2026 it remains fully entitled but unbuilt.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. This deliberately does NOT match today's satellite imagery of the parking lot -- this parcel's boundary represents the D4D's planned footprint, including '21ST ST (NEW)' and the '20th Street Plaza' open-space strip (data/manual/pier70_pkn_frontage_plaza.geojson), neither of which is built yet.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential, 65 ft max / 6 stories, 245 for-sale condominium units, 377,506 sf building, Handel Architects. Developer is TMG Partners + Presidio Bay Ventures -- NOT Brookfield; this parcel was purchased directly from the Port in Feb 2019 and is 'fully entitled' but has no confirmed groundbreaking as of the most recent research pass (2026).

facts.value: PKN Manager LLC, a subsidiary of TMG Partners, with Presidio Bay Ventures (joint venture buyer under the Vertical DDA); the Handel Architects page names the client as 64 PKN Owner, LLC
Sold by the Port; described by Presidio Bay as the only privately owned land in the Pier 70 Special Use District
approximately 68,800 sq ft (2017 Port memo); 1.5 acres (developer)
245 for-sale residential units (Port page); developer pages say 245 (TMG) and approximately 241 (Presidio Bay)
approximately 239 to 300 market-rate condominium units, about 6,600 sq ft of ground-floor retail/art/light-industrial space and about 186 parking spaces under the SUD (2017 memo)
377,506 gsf (Port page); 411,273 sq ft per Presidio Bay; 275,000 sq ft residential per TMG
maximum 147 off-street spaces, unbundled from units; at least 145 bicycle spaces; two car-share spaces (Planning conditions of approval)
A 20th St/Illinois St plaza and improvements to Michigan Street (Port page); the 2017 plan carved a separate 'Plaza Parcel' out of the 20th/Illinois parcel
'Fully entitled'; Handel lists the project as 'In Design'

open_questions: The purchase price: the only figure found is the Port's '$24.2 million of land proceeds from the sale of Parcel K North in February 2019'; the executed Vertical DDA and the Budget and Legislative Analyst report attached to File 190055 were not opened.

No groundbreaking or building permit was found. Bisnow's June 2019 piece says TMG and Presidio Bay 'broke ground after recent purchase', which conflicts with the Port page's 2020-2021 design-and-permitting timeline and with the November 2025 Potrero View report that no Pier 70 housing has materialized; treat the 2019 claim as unverified.

Affordable housing on PKN: the 2017 memo calls the units market-rate and the 2026 report says condo projects pay an in-lieu fee toward the stand-alone affordable sites, while the Planning conditions reference Section 415 affordable units; the actual obligation is unresolved.
Unit and square-footage figures disagree between the Port page (245 units, 377,506 gsf) and the two developer pages (241 units / 411,273 sq ft; 275,000 sq ft residential).
